migration_notes: 2026-06-13: Added additive saga_lifecycle block derived from the vendored saga-docs-model.yaml snapshot (plugin 0.21.0). At that migration, this was strictly additive and existing consumers (for example, wip_limits.olympus) were unchanged; superseded for Olympus routing by the 2026-06-17 retirement.

2026-06-13.2: Merged hand-authored config/saga-lifecycle-extras.yaml (combinations, reset_edges, gate_classification, phase_board_map, phase_command_map) into the saga_lifecycle block. Strictly additive; snapshot-derived keys and existing consumers unchanged.

2026-06-17: Retired Mount Olympus as an active board projection. phase_board_map now projects only Jeff Intent, Asgard, and CAMPPS; Project #1 is closed externally and preserved as historical context.
2026-07-10: Pinned Objective-field membership, Objective-grouped views, top-level-by-default Capabilities, and optional Outcome parents for explicit long-lived initiative-board contracts.
2026-07-18: Recorded Olympus-era remote repositories as retired-preserved entities. This is entity metadata only: saga lifecycle and active board vocabulary remain unchanged.

2026-08-16: Reduced every active board to Status / Objective / Priority and migrated CAMPPS onto the shared intent_flow ladder (Committed -> Ready, Parked -> Idea, In Progress removed). phase_board_map.campps now projects the same six columns as Operations and Asgard, so no lifecycle phase collapses onto a shared column any more. workflows.campps_initiative is retired-preserved, not deleted.

2026-08-28: Added the hand-authored lifecycle_field_mutation block (issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#87): the single constrained Mission Control lifecycle-field mutation writes only Stage and Status, resolves carrying boards from the issue's own projectItems, is all-carrying-boards-or-none atomic, halts and raises on a failed compensating write, and carries no transition-legality constraint. Authored contract only: no runtime consumer reads this block; the plugin enforces its own CORRECTION_FIELDS literal.

2026-08-28: Renamed the human-operator routing identifier teams.jeff to teams.operations, so approvals and decision requests route to the operator role rather than to a named person. boards.operations.owner now resolves to the operations team key, and human_approval_state.active_pattern requests the operator instead of a person. The team entry's kind, status, role, board, and review_model are unchanged, no alias for the old key remains, and historical records are preserved unchanged.

2026-08-28: Added responsibilities, default_assignment_patterns, independent_review, and authorization_boundary sub-blocks inside human_approval_state. Strictly additive: active_pattern, retired_patterns, and approval_required_for (the single separately-authorized-category list) are unchanged.

2026-08-28: Recorded decision D-A on issue #98 -- no new deployment-visibility project field is created on any board; the six documented names are preserved as documented-not-created vocabulary under deployment_state.visibility_fields. Added deployment_state.promotion_plan requiring every production promotion to carry a durable seven-part deployment plan (exact version, production target, prerequisites, rollback procedure, production verification, responsible actor, explicit production approval) at docs/deployments/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<target>-<version>.md in the promoting repository, with the plan file refused by tools/docs/check_deployment_plan.py when any element is missing. GitHub Deployments/Environments remain the authoritative deployment record.

2026-08-28: W18 (issue #99) recorded the Saga Code Review review-artifact publication lane in review_model (interactive mode only; evidence-only commit naming the reviewed revision as a full SHA; no implementation-edit authority) and answered Q6 as implementation_route: skill_contract_change_alone, no new registered operation kind. The Proceed / Revise / Block verdict vocabulary is retired from live documentation in the same change; dated records keep it.

2026-08-28: Added the hand-authored verify_entry block: the Verify entry condition (merge plus a succeeded non-production deployment; for work with no deployable software, the delivered artifact in its consumption context), the pre-merge-stays-Active rule, and the Active-versus-Verify test placement axis keyed on target and timing (R69/R70/R71). Strictly additive; existing keys unchanged.

2026-08-29: W13 (issue #94) landed the board-stage vocabulary: a new workflows.stage_flow carries the six Stage columns (Intake, Shaping, Planning, Active, Verify, Retro), the six per-stage Status sets with cross-cutting Blocked (26 distinct options), and terminal semantics; all three active boards re-point to it and fields gain Stage alongside Status. workflows.intent_flow keeps its preserved statuses but is canonical_for [] and superseded_by stage_flow (its removal is W11's); campps_initiative is untouched. boards.operations.routing_required_at moved off the retired Ready, and pause_states.source_note no longer describes Blocked as retired. The wip_limits block is marked non-authoritative in the same change.

2026-08-29: Added the hand-authored gate_catalogue block (issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#85): one versioned machine-readable catalogue of 47 gates, each carrying the six R20 attributes (evidence, applicability, owner, classification, override policy, failure route) plus id, source, classification_basis, and x7_ref for verifiability. Membership is X7's 44-row working set (docs/reviews/2026-08-29-x7-findings.md) plus the three deploy-plugin rows. Classification is advisory (the default), blocking (only where the gate's contract names mandatory evidence or a safety boundary), or the explicit string unclassified - an unclassified gate pauses for an operator decision, never silently blocking or advancing. The executable projection lives at tools/docs/gate_catalogue.py; the generated rendering at docs/process/gate-catalogue.md. Strictly additive: saga_lifecycle (including gate_classification, W11's custody) and every other block are unchanged.
description: Canonical Infiquetra SDLC board, team, routing, review, approval, and deployment-state schema. This file intentionally contains no live GitHub Projects field option IDs; tooling must resolve those from GitHub at runtime.

operations.role: Sole human operator, intent source, approval gate, escalation arbitrator, and occasional direct implementer with local AI tools

asgard.role: Jeff-proximal rapid-action, incubation, and mission-mode team with an issue-backed feed and lightweight proof model
asgard.modes_note: These three modes are an Asgard operating concept (docs/process/asgard-operating-model.md), not a project field. The Mode single-select was deleted from the Asgard board on 2026-08-16; nothing records a card's mode on the board any more.

olympus.role: Former primary autonomous engineering execution pipeline. Preserved for history only; do not route active work or current board state through Mount Olympus.

hermes.role: Hermes Agent framework and neutral capability contract used by active teams; distinct from the retired Team Hermes repository and its former plan-phase authority

team-hermes.role: Former Olympus-era plan-phase crew and deployment authority. Its remote repository is preserved, but it is not an active team or runtime owner.

themis.role: Former PR-review state machine. Preserved for migration history only; not an active routing path.

operations.name: Operations
operations.purpose: Raw operator intent, approvals, questions, personal/operator work, and shaping before team execution

asgard.name: Asgard
asgard.purpose: Rapid action, incubation, and mission-mode work close to Jeff

campps.name: CAMPPS
campps.purpose: Portfolio-level execution board for the CAMPPS program, tracking Outcome, Capability, and Component slice progress while the initiative is active
campps.archive_trigger: Operator declares the initiative complete after Objectives are Done and Outcome Scorecards are reviewed.

intent_flow.no_pause_state: No active board carries a pause column. CAMPPS's Parked was retired on 2026-08-16 and was not replaced; a paused card is represented by labels and issue state, not by a Status option.

stage_flow.note: R66 (board-stage migration W13): Stage is the board column field; Status carries the in-stage condition. The per-stage sets below are the authoritative structured fact; the retired names Idea, Ready and Done do not survive as Status values anywhere.
stage_flow.entry_option_rule: The first name in each stage_statuses list is the entry option: defaulting there invents no recorded progress (R49). Ready for Active (Planning) and Ready to close (Verify/Retro) are terminal exceptions that preserve recorded progress.
stage_flow.status_scoping: A GitHub single-select field cannot scope options per stage, so each board's Status field carries the flat 26-option union and the per-stage sets are authoritative only here. No defensive mechanism blocks a manual out-of-stage choice (R42); consistency is descriptive.

campps_initiative.retirement_note: Former CAMPPS-only lightweight ladder. Migrated onto intent_flow on 2026-08-16: Committed -> Ready (145 cards), Parked -> Idea (49 cards), In Progress removed (0 cards). The statuses array is preserved so historical cards, plans, and reviews naming these columns remain resolvable; it does not describe any live board.

work_hierarchy.source_note: Canonical machine-readable hierarchy for Objective, Outcome, Capability, and Component slice roles. Component is a dispatch role encoded by sub-issue position plus fields, not a separate issue type.

objective.supporting_artifact: Outcome Scorecard doc in the owning context-library repository
objective.membership_rule: Assign the Objective field value to every contributing Capability and executable child; do not create an Objective parent issue.

outcome.purpose: Dated proof tier for initiative-level outcomes when a long-lived initiative board exists.

capability.parent_policy: Top-level by default; use an Outcome parent only when the active board contract explicitly requires dated proof cards.
capability.purpose: Coordinates the end-to-end result across services and names the verification slice that proves completion.

encoded_by: native GitHub sub-issue position under a Capability
the slice's declared test strategy in the issue body (formerly the Test Strategy project field, deleted 2026-08-16)
component.purpose: Independently service-testable slice an agent can build inside one repository or bounded context.

component_slices.retired_field_record: Deleted from CAMPPS (Project #4) on 2026-08-16, destroying 284 field values. It had been verified live earlier the same day (single-select, options endpoint/event/schema/property/combine, 284 of 831 cards carrying a value; source tools/board/snapshot.py capture project-4-20260816T040238), and that capture is the snapshot of record at ~/.infiquetra/board-snapshots/. The five strategies below remain the verification doctrine for Component slices; only the board field that recorded the choice is gone. A slice now declares its strategy in the issue body.

endpoint.proof_expectation: Request and response seam proof for one endpoint vertical.

event.proof_expectation: Event emission, idempotency, state transition, and alarm or retry proof.

schema.proof_expectation: Schema invariant, compatibility, and generated artifact proof.

property.proof_expectation: Property, exhaustiveness, or state-space proof for non-enumerable behavior.

combine.proof_expectation: Cross-repository or cross-service seam proof that local green checks did not miss the end-to-end result.

component_slices.capability_close_rule: Every Capability coordinator names one enforced end-to-end verification slice before close; use combine when a cross-repo seam exists or a dedicated closeout E2E slice otherwise.

pause_states.source_note: Vocabulary of pause reasons, NOT a list of board columns. As of 2026-08-16 no active board carries a pause column at all: CAMPPS's Parked was the last one and was migrated into Idea. Needs Review and Needs Question are retired Mount Olympus column names kept as vocabulary. Blocked is NOT a pause state here: since the 2026-08-29 Stage migration it is a live cross-cutting Status, available in any Stage rather than belonging to one (R66). A paused card on an active board is expressed by labels and issue state.
pause_states.Plan-Approved: Plan accepted but operator intentionally paused dispatch.
pause_states.Needs Review: Operator or team review needed before work can continue.
pause_states.Needs Question: Author or operator input needed; currently treated as a human-input state.

wip_limits.source_note: NOT a live limit source. Marked non-authoritative 2026-08-29 (W13 board-stage migration): these keys are the retired six-column Status vocabulary (Idea, Shaping, Ready, Active, Verify, Done), which the Stage migration renamed out of existence. The per-board sub-objects are preserved byte-identical as a historical record; re-deriving limits for the Stage vocabulary is deliberately deferred and must not happen as a side effect. Do not direct agents here as a limit source.

Ready: Issue body satisfies the card contract (docs/process/card-schema.md), enforced by mission-control at creation

Active: UNKNOWN: both prior gates were backed by project fields deleted on 2026-08-16 (Mode must be set; Jeff Needed must be set when work crosses an approval boundary). No replacement gate has been decided. Operator call required; do not infer one.

Ready: Outcome or Capability is admitted to the initiative portfolio
Active: UNKNOWN: the prior In Progress gate required Component slices to identify their Test Strategy, and the Test Strategy field was deleted on 2026-08-16. No replacement gate has been decided. Operator call required; do not infer one.

team_routing.operations_ready_rule: A Ready Operations card must satisfy the card contract before moving to another board or workflow. Routing to a surface is an explicit operator action, not a field value.
team_routing.asgard_issue_feed_rule: Asgard-bound work enters by an operator routing an Operations card to Asgard, a direct issue added to Asgard, or a context/issue pack. The former pre-Active field checklist (Mode, target repository or surface, risk, approval state, proof path, transfer target) is void: every field backing it was deleted from the board on 2026-08-16. Mode, target surface, risk, and transfer intent now live in the issue body per the card contract (docs/process/card-schema.md), not in project fields.
team_routing.cross_team_transfer_rule: Asgard and CAMPPS are sibling active target surfaces. Cross-team movement happens only when an operator explicitly routes, transfers, clones, or links work to another board; readiness checks may warn about target fit but must not infer movement. Mount Olympus is retired historical context and is not an active target.
team_routing.default_pressure_valve: Prefer project views over new boards unless scale, automation, or reporting needs justify a separate board.

review_model.team_owned_review: The team that owns the work owns PR review, evidence, and merge readiness. Hermes may coordinate events, but does not route active PR review to Themis.
review_model.plan_review: Hermes can coordinate plan review before dispatch.
review_model.publication_lane: The Saga Code Review publication lane, granted in interactive / standalone mode only: the reviewer may write, commit, and push its own review document and submit the GitHub pull-request review. The lane grants no implementation-edit authority over reviewed source and is bounded to the review artifact's own path (docs/code-reviews/ plus the evidence ledger under docs/evidence/). A review-artifact commit is evidence only and records the exact implementation revision reviewed as a full 40-character commit SHA in the artifact frontmatter (reviewed_revision). Programmatic / report-only mode keeps its zero-durable-writes contract, which the Work staleness gate depends on.
review_model.repair_custody: The reviewer does not implement the fixes it requests. Findings route to the author or the Work process, which own repair changes and implementation commits.
review_model.implementation_route_note: Q6 answer, decided 2026-08-28: granting the lane requires no new registered operation kind in the safety allowlist and no widening of an existing one. The plugin's OpKind registry mirrors mission-control verbs, intentionally excludes repo-level mutations, and is default-deny, so the lane is bounded by the skill contract and the reviewer's toolset. Recorded with rationale in docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md.

retired.Themis: Historical PR-review state machine. Do not route active PR review to Themis from current SDLC docs.
retired.Proceed__Revise__Block verdict vocabular: The earlier three-way review verdict vocabulary is retired (source requirement R76, issue #99). Live documents express review results with the real Saga counterpart's vocabulary: the four typed review_result.v1 outcomes for PR review, and the one-line readiness verdict plus P0-P3 finding priorities for plan review. Historical use survives only in dated records (brainstorms, ideation notes, reviews).

human_approval_state.active_pattern: Per-agent direct message or per-card thread request to the operator, depending on the work context.
approval_required_for: major team or process authority changes

author.definition: The actor who writes the plan, design, or change under review.

implementer.definition: The actor that carries out an authorized change to completion.

integration_owner.definition: The actor accountable for integrating an approved change into the shared branch.

deployment_owner.definition: The actor accountable for releasing an approved change to a target environment.

verifier.definition: An independent actor that confirms acceptance evidence for a change.

independent_reviewer.definition: An independent actor that reviews material code or design it did not author.

independent_review.solo_operator_satisfied_by: an independent agent acting as a distinct actor

visibility_fields.decision: no new deployment-visibility project field is created on any board
visibility_fields.rationale: None of the six documented names exists on any board, verified read-only on 2026-08-28, and creating one would add a competing source of truth against GitHub Deployments for no named decision use.

documented_not_created.Deploy Target: Environment or promotion target requested by the work item
documented_not_created.Deploy State: Current deployment or promotion state derived from deployment records
documented_not_created.Snapshot Version: Immutable version or tag promoted across environments
documented_not_created.Promotion Pending: Whether a promotion approval or gate is waiting
documented_not_created.Release Risk: Operational risk classification for the release or promotion
documented_not_created.Last Deployment: Most recent deployment evidence link or timestamp

promotion_plan.location_convention: docs/deployments/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<target>-<version>.md in the promoting repository, linked from the issue
promotion_plan.refusal_rule: A production promotion is refused when its issue does not link a deployment plan at the location convention carrying a non-placeholder body under every required element; the plan file itself is refused by tools/docs/check_deployment_plan.py when a required element is missing, duplicated, or left as template placeholder.

exact_version.heading: Exact version
exact_version.description: The immutable version or tag being promoted to production

production_target.heading: Production target
production_target.description: The production environment or host the promotion lands on

prerequisites.heading: Prerequisites
prerequisites.description: Conditions that must hold before the promotion may start

rollback_procedure.heading: Rollback procedure
rollback_procedure.description: The concrete steps that undo the promotion

production_verification.heading: Production verification
production_verification.description: The checks that prove the promotion worked in production, not just in CI

responsible_actor.heading: Responsible actor
responsible_actor.description: The one actor accountable for executing and verifying the promotion

production_approval.heading: Production approval
production_approval.description: The explicit operator authorization for this promotion, recorded before it starts

deployment_state.display_owner: mission-control may display or link deployment state in a later pass

lifecycle_field_mutation.writable_fields_note: The single constrained Mission Control lifecycle-field mutation may write only these two fields; any other field name is rejected before a board is touched. Authored contract, not read at runtime: the plugin enforces its own CORRECTION_FIELDS literal.
lifecycle_field_mutation.board_discovery_note: Carrying boards are resolved from the issue's own projectItems, never from a repo-to-board mapping.
lifecycle_field_mutation.atomicity_note: Either every board carrying the issue ends at the new value, or every board ends at the value it held before the call.
lifecycle_field_mutation.transition_legality_note: No Stage or Status ladder exists and none may be added: no transition is rejected because an intermediate value was never occupied, backward movement is permitted whenever it truthfully represents current activity with the reason recorded, and no reconcile pass back-fills an unoccupied value.

gate_catalogue.source_note: Hand-authored per the W4 plan (issue infiquetra/infiquetra-sdlc#85). Membership is X7's 44-row working set plus the three deploy-plugin rows, transcribed row-by-row from the census. Classification enum: advisory (the default), blocking (only where the gate's own contract names mandatory evidence or a safety boundary), and the explicit string unclassified (the gate pauses for an operator decision - it never silently blocks and never silently advances). Every blocking row's classification_basis opens with the P14 trigger that justifies it ("Mandatory evidence:" or "Safety boundary:"); an unclassified row's classification_basis records why no verdict could be reached.

planning_to_active.note: Both are unclassified (self-declared UNKNOWN in dispatch_gates). The Operations board has no Active gate entry at all - an explicit absence recorded on docs/process/gate-catalogue.md, not an invented row. See the plan's UNKNOWN-1.

code_review_acceptance.note: R26's 'code-review acceptance' names the gate that decides PR acceptance - team-owned-pr-review (blocking, overridable: none). Saga's internal /code-review is catalogued separately as saga-code-review (advisory to the lifecycle phase). Plan KTD5.

approval_boundary_safety.note: P22 categories mapped: production changes (production-deployment-safety, deploy-autonomy-posture, deploy F1-F3), destructive actions and external commitments and changes to process authority (no-force-push, outward-github-mutation-confirmation, automation-eligibility-gate, tier-escalation-confirmation). Two of P22's six categories - credentials and identity, material spending - have an approval boundary in human_approval_state.approval_required_for but no pass/fail gate to catalogue; recorded as a known gap (the W4 plan's UNKNOWN-2). Minting gates for them would edit human_approval_state and invent contracts.

docs-gate-unit-tests.evidence: The checker/generator scripts behave per their own test fixtures
docs-gate-unit-tests.applicability: Every run of docs-gate.yml (PRs or main pushes touching docs/**, config/**, tools/docs/**, README.md, AGENTS.md, or the workflow itself)
docs-gate-unit-tests.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: the workflow's own header contracts the staged docs gate to "FAILS (does not warn)", so a passing unit-test step is mandatory evidence the job requires.

docs-gate-internal-links.evidence: Every relative markdown link inside a navigable docs/** file resolves against its containing file's directory
docs-gate-internal-links.applicability: Navigable docs only (tools/ is never walked)
docs-gate-internal-links.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: the workflow's own header contracts the staged docs gate to "FAILS (does not warn)" on broken internal links.

docs-gate-frontmatter-badge.evidence: Every navigable doc carries valid YAML frontmatter and its visible status badge matches the frontmatter's stability field
docs-gate-frontmatter-badge.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: the workflow's own header contracts the staged docs gate to "FAILS (does not warn)" on missing/invalid frontmatter.

docs-gate-schema-parity.evidence: config/sdlc-schema.json's generator-owned blocks (saga_lifecycle, issue_fields) match what regenerating from their vendored source would produce
docs-gate-schema-parity.failure_route: CI job fails red; the check is schema-to-snapshot only and structurally cannot see snapshot-to-live-plugin drift (X7 A7)
docs-gate-schema-parity.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: the workflow's own header contracts the staged docs gate to "FAILS (does not warn)" on schema-to-snapshot drift.

docs-gate-render-currency.evidence: The generated region in docs/process/gates.md (and sibling reconciliation docs) matches what the generator would currently produce
docs-gate-render-currency.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: the workflow's own header contracts the staged docs gate to "FAILS (does not warn)" on schema-to-snapshot drift, which for generated regions is a stale render.

docs-gate-llms-txt.evidence: docs/llms.txt (the agent-facing doc manifest) matches current frontmatter
docs-gate-llms-txt.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: the workflow's own header contracts the staged docs gate to "FAILS (does not warn)" on a stale llms.txt manifest.

docs-gate-plugin-reachability.evidence: The live installed Saga plugin's state_axes.lifecycle_phase.values equals the vendored snapshot's, and the live plugin.json version equals the pin in config/saga-plugin-pin.yaml
docs-gate-plugin-reachability.applicability: Only meaningful when the plugin is actually installed at check time
docs-gate-plugin-reachability.override_policy: --require-plugin makes absence a failure; when the plugin is present, default mode already fails on enum or version drift. The workflow never passes the flag.
docs-gate-plugin-reachability.failure_route: Silent skip-clean (exit 0) on every actual GitHub run (plugin absent); locally with the plugin installed, default mode already exits 1 on pin drift
docs-gate-plugin-reachability.classification_basis: Advisory-in-practice: the script's own docstring contracts SKIP-CLEAN (exit 0) when the plugin is absent, and GitHub-hosted runners never have it installed, so no mandatory-evidence or safety-boundary trigger holds on the runs that matter.

doc-review.evidence: Unresolved P0/P1 findings against a plan or requirements doc (P0 = unsafe/incorrect/destructive/materially wrong execution; P1 = a missing or wrong core assumption, mapping, requirement, default, or gate)
doc-review.owner: Not a named role - the reviewing agent holds the verdict
doc-review.override_policy: Recorded rationale, attached to the issue's durable record
doc-review.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: the gate's contract names unresolved P0/P1 findings as evidence that blocks /work (gate_classification.doc-review blocking: true; saga-docs-model.yaml: "P0/P1 findings block /work without recorded override").

saga-code-review.evidence: The serialized review_result.v1 envelope's outcome field (accepted / repairs_requested / cycle_cap_best_available / review_incomplete) - a typed outcome, not a finding count
saga-code-review.owner: Not stated; explicitly not the transport/orchestration layer
saga-code-review.override_policy: Recorded rationale (flows through the consumer contract's --doc-review-override flag)
saga-code-review.failure_route: Does not itself move the saga phase; feeds PR-ready status instead (repairs_requested routes back to Work)
saga-code-review.classification_basis: Advisory to the lifecycle-phase transition by contract: gate_classification.code-review carries blocking: false, advances_phase: false; the repository's own docs say it is an internal quality lens, not the authoritative pre-merge gate, and X7 records no P14 safety-boundary or mandatory-evidence language for it here.

qa-verify-evidence.evidence: Per-risk-class severity findings against a tier's blocking threshold (Quick: critical+high; Standard: +medium; Exhaustive: all)
qa-verify-evidence.override_policy: ship-with-deferred is the recorded-rationale path for non-blocking findings
qa-verify-evidence.failure_route: Verdict ship / ship-with-deferred / no-ship; no-ship keeps lifecycle_phase=work for repair
qa-verify-evidence.classification_basis: Explicitly advisory: the schema notes it as "advisory to the team-owned gate" - a no-ship verdict keeps lifecycle_phase=work for repair rather than hard-stopping anything.

plan-review.evidence: Problem-frame clarity; explicit scope boundaries; requirement traceability to an origin artifact; concrete file paths/verification expectations; named human-approval boundaries; deployment state separate from workflow status; no routing through retired review systems
plan-review.owner: The owning team remains accountable for the review outcome; Hermes only coordinates the event
plan-review.failure_route: Proceed / Revise / Block; Revise and Block require evidence plus a requested fix or decision
plan-review.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: review_model.plan_review is a blocking gate ("blocks dispatch") whose Revise/Block verdicts require findings with evidence.

team-owned-pr-review.evidence: Implementation matches the accepted plan (or divergence is explained); relevant tests/verification ran; docs/schema updated when behavior or process changed; deployment/approval boundaries understood; blocking findings carry concrete evidence and a requested change
team-owned-pr-review.owner: The team or initiative surface that owns the work - explicitly not Hermes, not the retired Themis
team-owned-pr-review.failure_route: Proceed / Revise / Block; Revise and Block require findings with evidence
team-owned-pr-review.source: config/sdlc-schema.json saga_lifecycle.gate_classification.team_owned_review; review_model.current = team_owned_review; docs/reviewers/pr-review.md; AGENTS.md Reviews rule
team-owned-pr-review.classification_basis: Safety boundary: the only gate in the census whose contract states no rationale-based override exists at all (blocking: true, overridable: false - "not unilaterally overridable; the owner decides"); it is the repository's authoritative pre-merge gate, so merge is its safety boundary.

card-contract-at-creation.evidence: The issue body against validate_card_body's card-contract schema
card-contract-at-creation.applicability: Issue creation, and enforcement at creation time (refusal of labels and board membership); same gate corroborated from docs/process/card-schema.md and mission-control's flow skill
card-contract-at-creation.owner: the orchestrator (enforced by mission-control at creation)
card-contract-at-creation.failure_route: Refused labels and board membership at creation; the CLI exits non-zero if the card body fails validation
card-contract-at-creation.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: a failing card body is refused, not warned - explicit enforcement language in card-schema.md ("refused labels and board membership at creation time").

campps-ready-admission.evidence: Outcome or Capability is admitted to the initiative portfolio; Objective field is set
campps-ready-admission.classification_basis: Mandatory evidence: two named, testable conditions gate admission to the state.

asgard-active-gate.evidence: UNKNOWN in the source itself: both prior gates were backed by project fields deleted on 2026-08-16 (Mode must be set; Jeff Needed must be set when work crosses an approval boundary)
asgard-active-gate.failure_route: Not defined - the schema's own text records no replacement gate
asgard-active-gate.classification_basis: UNCLASSIFIED, self-declared in dispatch_gates.asgard.Active: "No replacement gate has been decided. Operator call required; do not infer one." Corroborated by docs/process/asgard-operating-model.md ("Whether reaching Active is still gated on these being present is undecided").

campps-active-gate.evidence: UNKNOWN in the source itself: the prior In Progress gate required Component slices to identify their Test Strategy, and the Test Strategy field was deleted on 2026-08-16
campps-active-gate.failure_route: Not stated in the source (the gate's replacement is undecided)
campps-active-gate.classification_basis: UNCLASSIFIED, self-declared in dispatch_gates.campps.Active: "No replacement gate has been decided. Operator call required; do not infer one." A different deleted-field story than asgard-active-gate (Test Strategy, not Mode / Jeff Needed).

authorized-author-allowlist.evidence: Whether the author of an orchestrated card is on the authorized_humans allowlist
authorized-author-allowlist.applicability: Card intake by the Hermes orchestrator's eligibility check (intake frozen 2026-07-18)
authorized-author-allowlist.classification_basis: UNCLASSIFIED by W4's transcription judgment, flagged in the plan's Open Questions: X7 records it "dormant by inference, not explicitly retired" - a lifecycle status, not a P14 classification verdict, because the source text does not use the word retired for this sub-gate. R24's pause is the honest handling of a row whose lifecycle status is unsettled.

wip-limits.evidence: Card count per board-Status column against a configured numeric limit

verify_entry.description: Single authority for the Active/Verify boundary: the condition under which a work item may enter Verify, and whether a check belongs to Active or Verify. Prose documents link here and must not restate this contract (R10).
verify_entry.resolver_note: Resolved by tools/docs/verify_entry.py for reviewers and any automated consumer. The Stage write itself is W6's constrained Mission Control mutation; the causing-evidence inventory is X1's audit.
verify_entry.evidence_audit: docs/reviews/2026-08-29-x1-findings.md Inventory A transition T5 (Active -> Verify)
verify_entry.causing_evidence: For work with deployable software: a merged change plus a succeeded non-production deployment record. For work with no deployable software: the delivered artifact existing in its real form in the consumption context that must be evaluated. None of these may be fabricated (R71/EE8).
verify_entry.recording_operation: Mission Control's constrained lifecycle-field mutation (W6's authored contract, landed 2026-08-28): one atomic all-carrying-boards-or-none Stage/Status write resolving carrying boards from the issue's own projectItems. Today's live mechanism is `flow set-field --correction` reached through the reconcile controller's set-field-status op. Verify is never written pre-merge (X1 audit, Central Mechanism; T5).

deployable_work.note: Verify is entered only after merge plus a succeeded non-production deployment. A failed or missing deployment leaves the item in Active (R69).

pre_merge_stays_active.note: Pre-merge CI, tests, code review, and PR-ready never advance the Stage to Verify (R69/R2).

no_deployable_software.require_merge_note: Verify begins after merge for this class of work too; the R71 no-deployable route relaxes the deployment requirement, never the merge requirement (R69/R1).
no_deployable_software.verified_when: The delivered artifact exists in the real form and consumption context that must be evaluated: the rendered published page for documentation, the installed version for a plugin (R71/R6).

deploying_to_non_production.never_set_when: the work has no deployable software

no_deployable_software.note: Where deployment practice does not apply, the absence is recorded with a reason; no environment or deployment record may be fabricated to satisfy the transition (R71, EE8).

test_placement.description: Whether a check belongs to Active or Verify, keyed on its target and timing -- never on the label 'end-to-end' (R70/R5). A check whose target is an assembled candidate (an artifact built from the change, not yet deployed) at pre-merge or at-merge timing is Active; a check whose target is a deployed environment or the delivered artifact in its consumption context at post-deployment timing is Verify.

targets.assembled_candidate: An artifact built from the change (repository checkout, built/installed-from-source candidate) that has not been deployed to an environment.
targets.deployed_environment: A real (including non-production) environment the change has been deployed to.
targets.delivered_artifact_in_context: The delivered artifact in its real consumption context: the rendered published page for documentation, the installed version for a plugin.

timings.post_deployment: After the change is merged and deployed, or after the no-deployable-software artifact exists in its consumption context.

rule.unresolved: HALT: a target/timing combination the rule does not name raises rather than defaulting (HALT over degrade).

saga_lifecycle.source_note: Generated by tools/docs/gen_saga_schema.py from the vendored saga snapshot (config/saga-docs-model.yaml) merged with the hand-authored config/saga-lifecycle-extras.yaml. Snapshot-derived: phases, state_axes, maturity derivation, gates_raw. Extras-authored: combinations, reset_edges, gate_classification, phase_board_map, phase_command_map.

gates_by_command.office-hours: Never implement, plan, scaffold, or file an SDLC issue.
gates_by_command.ideate: Preserve rejection reasons; do not treat operator seed ideas as exempt from critique.
gates_by_command.brainstorm: Keep WHAT and acceptance examples clear enough for /plan.
gates_by_command.spec: Do not produce a spec after message 1; interrogate first and read code before technical questions.
gates_by_command.plan: Does not implement or run the review gauntlet.
gates_by_command.doc-review: P0/P1 findings block /work without recorded override.
gates_by_command.work: Hard test gate by risk; hard review gate on P0/P1 or stale review; PR and merge require confirmation.
gates_by_command.code-review: P0/P1 findings block PR-ready unless overridden.
gates_by_command.qa: Verdict threshold determines ship, ship-with-deferred, or no-ship.
gates_by_command.handoff: Ask when source, maturity, target repo, team, or issue type is ambiguous.
gates_by_command.retro: Self-edit safety gate; modifications/deletions require explicit apply/skip/modify choice.
gates_by_command.promote: Every context-library write is propose-diff-and-wait; idempotent via the drift-stable source-key ledger.
gates_by_command.resume: Read-only on world; Tier 2 session forensics only when no saga and no resolvable issue exist.
gates_by_command.investigate: No fix without root-cause chain grounded in observed evidence.
gates_by_command.optimize: Hard degenerate gates before any LLM judge; keep only real measured improvement.
gates_by_command.strategy: Interview-driven update with pushback; do not implement or file issues.
gates_by_command.loop: Enforces doc-review P0/P1 hard gate before /work; stub/off-chain routes are advisory.
gates_by_command.tier: An up-ladder mid-run escalation requires operator confirmation before re-emit; a ceiling only ever clamps down.
gates_by_command.outcome: Coordinator routes and dispatches but never runs leaf work; pages only at gates, unsatisfiable barriers, ambiguity, and parent-close.
gates_by_command.fleet-doctor: Absence, corruption, and incompleteness are distinct verdicts; any cap, corruption, unsafe path, or mid-scan change forces exit 2 and can never truncate to a clean report.
gates_by_command.pulse: Tri-state source honesty per panel (ok / no-data / unavailable, ledger adds chain-broken); a broken chain suppresses all aggregates; no thresholds, not a gate.
gates_by_command.engines: Pin targets must exist, declare the capability, and not be locally deprecated; route explain is read-only.

main_chain.reason: Turn idea or requirements context into HOW.
Execute only after no unresolved P0/P1 review findings or recorded override.
Capture lifecycle learning when work is complete.

legal.note: any phase can be handed off
plan finished, advancing to the review gate

illegal.reason: a done thread cannot have an in-progress phase
a done thread cannot have a pending phase (status=done requires phase_status=complete)

reset_edges.reason: Accepted scope change from founder-review routes back to /plan for a re-plan that re-runs /doc-review (model: founder-review.routes_out + doc-review.routes_out include /plan).
A stale base (the plan's assumptions diverged from a moved main) forces a re-plan before continuing work (saga-spec convention, not in the model).
A failed acceptance verdict keeps lifecycle_phase=work for repair routing (model: qa.saga_state_behavior 'on fail, keeps lifecycle_phase=work'; qa.routes_out includes /work).
Blocking code-review findings route back into the work loop before PR-ready (model: code-review.routes_out includes /work).

doc-review.source: saga-docs-model.yaml commands.doc-review.gates ('P0/P1 findings block /work without recorded override')
doc-review.note: Authoritative implementation-readiness gate; unresolved P0/P1 block /work; advances review -> work; overridable only with a recorded rationale.

code-review.note: Internal quality lens at the work->PR boundary, NOT a substitute for team-owned PR review; advisory in the authority sense; does not advance the lifecycle spine.

qa.source: saga-docs-model.yaml commands.qa (saga_state_behavior: 'on pass, advances qa-track'; gates: 'Verdict threshold determines ship, ship-with-deferred, or no-ship')
qa.note: Post-merge acceptance-evidence verdict; advisory to the team-owned gate; a passing verdict advances the thread qa->retro (the qa-track is recorded), a no-ship keeps lifecycle_phase=work; ship-with-deferred is the recorded-rationale path.

plan-review.source: config/sdlc-schema.json review_model.plan_review ('Hermes can coordinate plan review before dispatch')
plan-review.note: Hermes-coordinated plan readiness before dispatch; blocks dispatch; does not itself advance the stored lifecycle_phase (/plan completing does).

team-owned-pr-review.note: The authoritative PR review + merge-readiness gate; the team or initiative surface that owns the work owns it; clearing it (with merge) advances work->qa; not unilaterally overridable (the owner decides).

review.note: The doc-review gate is the Ready->Active gate on all three active boards (plan approved before work goes Active). CAMPPS joined this shared ladder on 2026-08-16; its former Committed column migrated to Ready.

work.note: Work (with code-review at the PR boundary) runs in Active on all three active boards.

qa.note: The qa verdict gates Verify -> Done on all three active boards. CAMPPS gained a separate Verify column on 2026-08-16; qa no longer shares a column with work on the initiative rollup.

retro.note: Learn (/retro) runs post-Done; no dedicated board column.

issue_fields.source_note: Generated by tools/docs/gen_issue_contract.py from the issue_fields block in config/sdlc-schema.json (U2: full field set, faithfully extracted from card_validator.py). DATA only -- the card_validator algorithm (home-lab) is never generated (KTD2).

Why this matters + the end-state (distinct from the one-line Objective), so the agent can re-derive the right action when the plan no longer applies.
Explicit list of things the agent MUST NOT do. If there are no non-goals, write "None" rather than leaving blank.
The countable inputs (files, IDs, endpoints, fixtures) confirmed to exist before step 1. Required for high-risk items.

Pre-mortem table: condition -> pre-authorized response (do-instead, not a bare don't). Required for high-risk items.
Explicit escalation triggers keyed to actions (when to stop and ask rather than proceed). Required for high-risk items.

Deep-links into the project's long-running context-library repo. Required: link the relevant context, or write `_none_` to declare no link applies. Use labeled subsections so policy-dependent reviewers know which doc applies.
